events.title: Check that image notifications preserve the nonce
events.body:
In test_image_embed_keeps_owner_target_and_nonce, add `self.assertEqual(args[1]['nonce'], 'nonce')`. The test currently checks `enforce_nonce` but does not check that the supplied nonce reaches the Discord request. Preserving it supports deduplication when a delivery is retried.
Run the existing test offline with its mocked Discord API. As a regression check, changing the request nonce to a different value or omitting it should make the new assertion fail.
The supplied test does not establish whether the implementation currently preserves the nonce. The proposed reliability claim would be falsified if Discord does not use that request field to deduplicate retries, or if retries do not reuse the same nonce. No code was executed.

events.title: Assert the exact nonce in the image notification test
events.body:
Ji An: Add self.assertEqual(args[1]['nonce'], 'nonce') to test_image_embed_keeps_owner_target_and_nonce. The supplied test checks enforce_nonce but never verifies the nonce value, despite its name. This strengthens coverage without changing live defaults.
Use the existing mocked Discord API; no network is needed. Cross-examination: enforce_nonce=True alone cannot establish that the supplied nonce survives. The added assertion should pass for the intended payload and fail if its nonce is omitted or replaced.
Production behavior is not shown, so no delivery defect is established. The proposal is falsified if the added assertion fails to distinguish correct nonce forwarding from an omitted or altered nonce. Tests were not executed.

events.title: Test delivery failure and retry behavior
events.body:
Add a deterministic test in `tests/test_notifications.py` for a queued alert when `Sender.send` raises: verify it stays pending and is delivered exactly once on a later successful tick. Existing tests cover duplicate suppression and delayed expiry, but not transient send failure; retry semantics are unverified here.
Use a fake sender that raises on its first call and succeeds on its second. Tick twice and assert two attempts, one recorded delivery, and no extra delivery after another tick.
The supplied test file does not establish the scheduler’s intended failure policy. This proposal is falsified if `Scheduler.tick` is documented or implemented to discard failed sends instead of retrying; inspect its source before making the test normative.
